Te-ai săturat să zâmbești forțat în prime-time-ul vieții tale? Fă o pauză. Aici, ai voie să fii un dezastru în direct.

Delilah este raza de soare de la știrile dimineții, care zâmbește colorat în timp ce inima ei este frântă de dor. Jackson este meteorologul morocănos de la radio, care își calculează viața în tabele Excel doar ca să nu lase atacurile de panică să-l sufoce.

Ea caută haosul pentru a supraviețui; el caută ordinea pentru a nu se prăbuși. N-ar trebui să funcționeze absolut deloc. Dar când un viscol istoric îi blochează într-o cabană minusculă, „jocul” lor de-a șoarecele și pisica se transformă într-o cursă contra cronometru cu propriile inimi.

O lectură pentru noi, cei care purtăm măști prea grele în fiecare zi și care nu avem toate lucrurile puse la punct. Lasă productivitatea toxică pentru mâine. Ai voie să iei o pauză. Ai voie să nu fii bine tot timpul. Descoperă povestea în care tensiunea topește orice barieră și lasă-te convinsă că, uneori, cea mai mare furtună este, de fapt, drumul tău spre liniște.

Savurează o dinamică electrică ce îți garantează fluturi în stomac și râs cu lacrimi, de la primul „Suntem în direct” până la ultima pagină.

* Refugiu mental garantat: Este biletul tău de ieșire dintr-o realitate hiper-stresantă. O lectură care îți oprește avalanșa de gânduri și îți oferă liniștea de care ai nevoie.

* Tropi irezistibili: Forced proximity într-o cabană izolată, enemies-to-lovers cu replici acide, tensiune electrică și „uraganul” care topește orice regulă.

* Personaje pe bune, nu clișee: Jackson și Delilah sunt obosiți, anxioși și încearcă doar să supraviețuiască unei noi zile. Te vei regăsi în fiecare zâmbet forțat și în fiecare mască pe care o poartă.

* Aprobarea reginelor romance-ului: O carte lăudată de autoare precum Julia Quinn și Sophie Cousens, fiind deja considerată „cea mai amuzantă și vindecătoare comedie romantică a anului”.

Thank you so much to Netgalley for providing this ARC!

Oh, B.K. Borison has done it again (as we knew she would). I adore all of her other books, namely First Time Caller, so this was one of my most anticipated releases, and it did not disappoint!!

This book completely charmed me right from the get go. There’s an ease to the writing (as with all B.K. Borison books I feel) that makes it incredibly quick to read, but at the same time it doesn’t feel rushed. One of the main things I adored about this book was the the chemistry between our main characters - it comes across so naturally that it never felt forced/over the top/lust based, and it made me literally kick my feet and giggle at times (lol).

Our gorgeous MMC Jackson deserves his own paragraph because he’s literally that lovable and endearing. He’s written with the perfect mix of warmth, cuteness and lowkey vulnerability, which endeared him to me super quickly. Some of the quotes from his POV had me literally having to put down my kindle and stare at a wall for a bit - it was literally that serious🙂‍↕️ I fear he may be one of my new ultimate book boyfriends and I think it’ll take me a while to stop thinking about him LOL

The setting and the atmosphere were also wonderful - a lot of this takes place at a lodge in the middle of a snowstorm, which I felt gave this book a sense of coziness and intimacy and wintery-vibes that I absolutely loved.

Overall, this book is the perfect kind of read for when you want something cutesy but still meaningful and ‘deep’ in places, romantic but not cringey, and atmospheric enough make you feel like you are also at a snowy lodge with these characters. I was grinning ear-to-ear for majority of this book, and Jackson is the new blueprint. LOVED this book and would highly recommend you to pick it up once it comes out!!

I think I’m officially addicted to B.K. Borison’s new series. She’s always been a master at crafting adorable, whip-smart main characters—but this time she also serves up a villain so loathsome I wanted to turn him into a human punch-bag. From Keith’s first appearance, I was inventing increasingly creative curses to hurl at the page. My hatred for him briefly eclipsed my love for Jackson and Delilah (briefly!), and I kept wanting to wrap Delilah in a protective bubble because that woman deserves only good things.

The marketing nods to When Harry Met Sally made me grin, but what really stole the show are the tropes: forced proximity, grumpy-meets-sunshine, and opposites attract—all executed to perfection. Jackson became a parent figure far too young, raising his twin sisters like a single dad after being failed by a selfish, neglectful mother; he’s meticulous, controlled, and painfully selfless. Delilah, also abandoned by her mother and now caring for a grandfather whose memories are slipping away, is stuck under the thumb of an egotistical boss (hi, Keith) who sabotages her at every turn. Yet she keeps smiling, keeps showing up, even when it hurts. They carry different kinds of scars, but both are quietly heroic.

On the surface they couldn’t be more different. Delilah thrives in the spotlight—spontaneous, adventurous, a natural live reporter. Jackson hates cameras, clings to schedules, and breaks out in hives if someone rearranges his bullet points. Then comes the assignment: they must travel together to cover a historic—and frankly terrifying—snowstorm, filing stories from the eye of the blizzard. Cue the clashing styles, the snark, the slow warming. Jackson thinks Delilah is chaos in cute boots; Delilah thinks Jackson has forgotten how to have fun. What neither expects is how much they’ll learn about themselves while learning to work together.

The weather nerdery is a delight (two people flirting over radar models? Inject it into my veins), but it’s the emotional weather that matters: how each of them handles the metaphorical storms that shaped their lives. As miles and whiteout conditions pile up, walls come down. The banter is sparkling, the tenderness is earned, and the chemistry is the kind that fogs up windows. Somewhere between emergency broadcasts and roadside diners, “colleagues” becomes “friends,” and “friends” becomes…well, you’ll see. Let’s just say their forecast calls for undeniable.

Overall: I’m this close to launching an “I Hate Keith” merch line—T-shirts, mugs, the works—and mailing them out with copies of the book and a box of emergency, sprinkle-heavy cruffins. I haven’t loathed a character this much since Game of Thrones’ Joffrey and Ramsay. Thankfully, Delilah and Jackson’s sweetness (and those precious twins, Adeline and Penelope!) soothed my rage. This is another feel-good romance from B.K. Borison—one that lights up my heart like a string of Christmas lights and reminds me hope can survive the harshest weather, the worst bosses, and the messiest pasts. Five “let it snow” stars!

A very huge thanks to NetGalley and Berkley Publishing for sharing this extra-sweet, adorable romance’s digital reviewer copy with me in exchange for my honest thoughts.

Do I like it? Do I not like it? I haven’t felt this conflicted about a book in a while. I said I would sit on it to gain some perspective, but I have sat and sat on it. If I continue, the book might get crushed under the weight of my indecision, which means I will likely never rate it at all.

And Now, Back to You follows the story of Jackson and Delilah, two meteorologists who fall in love. If you’ve read First Time Caller, you’ll remember Jackson as a member of the Baltimore radio team who spills meteorological facts whenever he gets anxious. I was genuinely excited about him getting his own story because I love nerdy MCs. Even better when it’s a nerdy MMC in love.

I’ll be honest and say that I wasn’t blown away from the beginning, as even the MCs’ first on-page meeting felt like a cliché. However, I was content enough with how everything was unfolding to keep reading, at least up until the very first kiss.

Ordinarily, the setting and circumstances should have made it feel electric, but instead it felt… off to me. And things went downhill quickly from there. Then came the aftermath. Poor Delilah running endless circles in her head about what should’ve been an exciting moment. I love reading about people stumbling and fumbling into love. I enjoy watching characters who do not quite know what they are doing fall into each other anyway. Here, though, it simply wasn't well executed. They had multiple discussions, attempting to articulate their attraction and clarify their relationship, yet the result was always confusing even for me as a reader. People, it’s really not that hard. Why abuse the English language? Why must it suffer for your love?

I know, I know. It’s predictable that Jackson, who is always so put together and in control, doesn’t quite know what to do when he’s no longer guided by strict agendas and timetables. That fits his character and it’s a lovely idea, but I still wish he had been written more as a take-charge hero. That is why I read romance. I want to see love drag people out of their shells into unknown places. I want it to burn through their defenses, push them past their limits, and drive them into situations they would not naturally enter. I want to believe in the stories I read. But Jackson, true to his character comes across as annoyingly passive, which then causes the FMC to question herself repeatedly.

On the bright side, Delilah doesn’t hold it against him. His hesitation does come across as sweet at times. I also love the opposites-attract dynamic. Jackson, the meticulous planner, paired with Delilah, who feels like the reincarnation of a rogue train, is an intriguing contrast. If you love tortured MCs, you will definitely enjoy this, because between them there was just so much baggage to unpack:

🧳 Mummy issues 
🧳 Family issues 
🧳 Anxiety and Stage fright 
🧳 Impulsiveness 
🧳 Professional people pleasing 
🧳 Professional doormat 
🧳 Career troubles 
🧳 Workplace scandal

At the end of the day, I love B.K. Borison and I will read whatever she writes. That said, this book wasn’t quite what I expected, but I would still call it a good read. For me, it was the many clichés, the MMC, and my inability to invest in the characters’ relationship that kept it from being great. So, my initial reaction still stands. I suspect I would have been happier reading about these MCs in therapy rather than in whatever it was they were entangled in.



Initial reaction

I think I would’ve been happier reading about these MCs in therapy. I’m not even being sarcastic when I say that. I rooted for Delilah and Jackson, separately. But I suppose this worked too.
What I don’t like though, was how the book kept hitting clichés back to back. I don’t know. I think I need to sit with it a bit longer. I’m still not entirely sure what to make of how I feel, so for now, people of Goodreads, back to you.

B.K. does it again! There are a few other authors in the running, but I think with this book she might have taken the lead as my FAVORITE romance author! I loved Good Spirits and First-Time Caller a tiny bit more than this one, but the margin was very thin! What really makes B.K.’s work stand out to me is her ability to develop such rich and vibrant characterizations without allowing her writing to feel overly character driven. These MC’s had extremely different personalities, but she managed to make them both feel just as relatable. The way they cared for their family members made them both so easy to love!

I’ve been on the hunt for great “snowed in” romances and this one definitely tops the list! Their chemistry had been simmering under the surface for years, but they needed the forced proximity and secluded mountain setting to finally push them over the edge. They were crazy to think what had been building between them could ever be confined to that weekend, but they likely wouldn’t have been brave enough to act on their desires if they hadn’t convinced themselves they could go back to the way things were. I really loved how the author built this story! Everything about this book was just so good! I feel like I’m rambling a little, but this series is a must read!

Heartstrings #2
And Now, Back to You
By B.K. Borison

You can read this as a standalone but for the most fun, read the first book in this series, First-Time Caller, because both books contain the same characters and it's fun to see them throughout the two books. Working at a radio or TV station is fraught with perils and fun and things get even wilder when love interests become intertwined with work, as they do with this series.

Jackson Clark and Delilah Stewart are oil and water, opposites that don't attract, and each can be the worst of each other's day. Sure, if Jackson, the radio station weatherman didn't thrive on routine and organization and having every single thing in his life line up perfectly, maybe Delilah would barely be a blimp on the things that make him lose his cool in life. But no, Jackson notices when things aren't done the way he thinks they should be done which includes parking crookedly in the parking space next to his.

Delilah, from the TV station across the parking lot, is a mess in every single way. She can't walk five steps without out slinging food, liquids, whatever in every direction. Her boss, Keith, seems to hate her and he takes advantage of this hate by assigning Delilah humiliating TV spots rather than allowing her to present the weather in a professional manner. In fact, he doesn't want her to present the weather, at all.

Now Jackson and Delilah have been partnered to travel to the location of the snowstorm of the century. And, oops, thanks to some suspicious reservations mishaps, Delilah and Jackson are going to be spending ALL their time together during this assignment. Mr Organization and Ms Stuff It All in a Pile are going to be in one place! Jackson seems to abhor Delilah and Delilah loves pushing his stuck up buttons so this should be fun for someone.

The two actually have more in common than nothing since they each have unresolved issues that could use some serious therapy but that's not happening in this story. Responsible Jackson is the caretaker of his sisters and has been taking care of them his entire life. So does Jackson end up taking care of mess Delilah or does he run from one more responsibility? Delilah wants to do her job presenting the weather but so much is working against her in that area and it's so important that her grandfather get to see her on TV. She certainly can stand on her own two feet (well, not literally since she seems to fall so much) but fate might not allow her to do so.

Amongst all the not getting along between these two is simmering lust and this author doesn't hold back on the spice and open door romance when it arrives. It seems like these two should be magnets repelling each other but instead there seems to be something pulling them together even though they don't want to admit it. I never doubted certain things about these two, no matter how much they protest.

First of all, let me start by saying that I’m shocked by my rating, because I really thought this was going to be five stars for me. I loved Jackson in the first book and was waiting for his book—I genuinely thought his book was going to be five stars, but I was upset it wasn’t. Four stars is not a bad rating at all, it's just not what I was expecting to get from this book.

This book is so, so good, and I enjoyed it so much. I was even raving about it to my friends; however, the first book is much better in my opinion. The first book resonated with me more, and I related more to it than this one.

First-Time Caller had long chapters and a third-act breakup; this book doesn’t have those, which I loved. However, this book lacked in other aspects. There is no balance between the two books at all. This book lacks the emotional depth that the first book has. It doesn’t have any soul, if that makes sense. It doesn't feel like a 90s movie, the same way the first book does.

⁀જ➣꒰ ⋮ ρℓσт.꒱

The plot was so, so cute, and I really loved it. However, this book is not a memorable book by any means. First-Time Caller was a book I thought about for days because of the vibes, setting, and romance, but this one? It’s quite forgettable.

In fact, what started as a cute banter between the characters went downhill, and it felt repetitive at times. The inner monologues were almost the same, and they were worrying about their feelings instead of communicating. I mean, they did communicate with each other at times, which was a nice change. I just wish they communicated at ALL times. Their inner turmoil was quite repetitive.

Also, most importantly, this is NOT enemies to lovers. Jackson doesn’t even hate her, and he mentions that in the book. They just bicker for a few chapters, and that’s about it.

While First-Time Caller was a very slow burn, this book was quite the opposite. They fold for each other very early on in the book.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ 𝕽𝖔𝖒𝖆𝖓𝖈𝖊.꒱

I loved the romance between Delilah and Jackson, but I think Jackson needs to be taken care of even more. Don't get me wrong, I loved their relationship, I just wish someone had taken care of him more than he did. Yes, Delilah took care of him, but at a certain point in the book, I felt like she was adding more to his plate.

However, Jackson's way of showing his love is very heart-melting. Their vulnerability with each other was very genuine to witness. This book had physical touch as a love language, and the glimpses of that made the romance swoon-worthy.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ ᭙𝕣ⅈ𝕥ⅈꪀᧁ.꒱

The writing was good, not great. I feel like the writing in the first book was much better. The writing in the first one resonated with me much more and felt more relatable. I struggled to connect with this one emotionally.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Characters: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

જ⁀➴ Jackson: This man is so perfect, I could cry. He needs to be protected at all costs. The things he said had me swooning and giggling. His weather rambles were adorable. I adored him in the first book, and even more in this book. He is such a green flag—he's grumpy, but soft and gentle in the way he loves and cares. I loved seeing him take care of his siblings—he's so protective and devoted to them, it made my heart melt. I related to him in certain ways: how he cares for his siblings, how organised he likes to be, and even his anxiety at times. This man struggles with so much weight on his shoulders that he's scared of letting anyone down. And let's not forget his friendship with Aiden, it is everything to me. I love them both so much—they're so funny together.

She also felt bland at times, like I wasn't seeing much of her. However, putting that aside, she was a ray of sunshine in Jackson's life with her own battles and struggles that just wished to be taken seriously. It was nice seeing her interact with strangers and try to please them. I just wish she stood up to her boss sooner than when it happened in the book. However, I adored her relationship with her grandfather.

“𝑲𝒊𝒔𝒔 𝒎𝒆, 𝑫𝒆𝒍𝒊𝒍𝒂𝒉,” 𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒂𝒚𝒔. “𝑴𝒂𝒌𝒆 𝒊𝒕 𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒈𝒐 𝒂𝒘𝒂𝒚. 𝑷𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒆.”

I can't believe how amazing this book was!!!!! I haven't read a book with two characters who display such tenderness toward each other in a loooong time 🥹 I was in love with Delilah and Jackson from their first encounter, and they had me riding such a giddy high throughout the entire book. Delilah Stewart is a meteorologist for Baltimore's news station who is all smiles and loves being on TV. The only problem is that she isn’t taken seriously, so when a weather assignment is handed to her, her mission is to succeed and finally earn the recognition she deserves. The only issue? She has to work with Jackson Clark, the weatherman for the radio station, who wants nothing to do with Delilah… until he starts noticing her and how she affects him 😌

“And Now Back To You” tugged at my heartstrings just like the first in this series-“First Time Caller” 💞 If you enjoyed that one-you will enjoy this one too!

Two Words: Doughnut Sled

Yes, Delilah Stewart may have had Jackson Clark with those two little words, and he may have had her, when he was able to talk to her about lake effect snow and changing pressure systems!

But, their attraction was definitely NOT instantaneous.

Jackson thrives on routine and organization, at home while raising his two younger siblings, and at work-preferring to hide behind the mic 🎙️ of the radio booth, at Baltimore’s home for easy listening, 101.6 Lite FM.

Fellow meteorologist Delilah loves to report the weather, and whatever other stories her Boss assigns her, on TV 📺 knowing that her beloved Grandfather with Alzheimer’s is watching every broadcast.

Their opposing styles have been clashing for years in the parking lot shared by their respective employers, via Post It Notes.

But, with THE snowstorm of the century, bearing down on Baltimore, they find themselves assigned to cover the storm TOGETHER from out in the field.

Eager to be taken seriously as a journalist, Delilah agrees to the plan, but Jackson feels more anxious about the assignment.

That is until he begins to fall under her spell, as the rest of Baltimore has…

And, I was as SMITTEN with their story as they were for each other-from the opening page!

Book #2 in the Heartstrings series, checked all of the boxes for a romance with witty banter, red hot chemistry (a bit spicier than my personal preference) and lovable leads I was rooting for!

Tropes: Grumpy/Sunshine, Forced Proximity/One Bed, Enemies to Lovers

A great FIRST ROMANCE of the year, and I am eagerly awaiting the third (and final) book in the series due out in 2027. Whose story will it be? Perhaps Maggie and Cooper West? Or will it be Gianna? I can’t wait to find out!

✄┈ 𝘑𝘢𝘤𝘬𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘋𝘦𝘭𝘪𝘭𝘢𝘩, 𝘵𝘸𝘰 𝘳𝘪𝘷𝘢𝘭 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘰𝘳𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘴 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘰𝘱𝘱𝘰𝘴𝘪𝘵𝘦 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘦𝘴, 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘤𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘬 𝘵𝘰𝘨𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘶𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘮𝘢𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘷𝘦 𝘴𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘳𝘮. 𝘞𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘴 𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘱𝘦𝘵𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘴𝘭𝘰𝘸𝘭𝘺 𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘯𝘴 𝘪𝘯𝘵𝘰 𝘧𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘴𝘩𝘪𝘱—𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘰𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘣𝘭𝘺 𝘴𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘦. 📺

This book wasn’t anything special—it was simple and pretty predictable—but I still enjoyed it 🩵

There wasn’t much conflict between the main characters. Aside from the beginning, once feelings developed (which happened quite fast), any tension just disappeared. That’s also clear with the absence of a third-act breakup. Instead, the story focuses more on them dealing with their own personal struggles and supporting each other through it 🫶🏻

Jackson’s feelings developed a bit too quickly, and I didn’t fully understand how they started.
But honestly, what made up for that was how caring he is 🥹 Especially towards Delilah and his sisters. His protectiveness and sense of responsibility really stood out, and I loved how he always stepped up for them. What I appreciated most was his honesty—once he realized his feelings, he didn’t run or hide. He showed it through his actions and openly admitted it.
Jackson being an adorable grumpy?? I did NOT expect that at all based on the first book—I genuinely thought he was a sunshine type.

And Delilah… my poor girl, but she’s literally a walking chaos. 😂 I loved her so much, and I felt really bad for her—having to go through all of that just to keep her job as a weather presenter, only so her grandfather could see her on screen.

Overall: a simple, light read with lovable characters.

5 Stars ⭐️

"It's always been me coming right back to you. You’re the end of every sentence, Delilah. I've just been too stubborn to see it."


This was cute and heartfelt. It just wrapped itself around me in the best ways.

And Now Back to You is the second book in the Heartstrings series. I just knew this was going to be fun, especially once I realized it was a snowed-in situation with one bed. I was literally screaming with joy. I love both of these tropes. Then you throw in the forced proximity, opposites attract, and found family, and I was sold. What I also loved were the caregiver aspects. Borison navigated both of the situations with care and thoughtfulness. What really made this a great time is that the narration by Max Myers and Brittany Pressley had me fully immersed in this story.

Jackson and Delilah have had their fair share of run-ins over the years that often end in disaster. They are partnered together to cover a snowstorm and must work closely. Now they must figure out how to work together. The more time they spend working together, the more feelings start to surface for one another.


Jackson Clark I enjoyed his character in First Time Caller and just knew that I would enjoy him in this. What I wasn't expecting was to fall in love with him from the very first chapter. He is the sweetest, and the way that he cares for his sisters had my heart melting and swooning 🥰 I loved his random rambles when he was nervous and feeling anxious. The way that he likes to have a routine and be organized, because honestly, same. Delilah Stewart my sweet girl 🥹 I was worried at first, as she is a bit of a people pleaser, but with her, I wasn't bothered by it. Everything else about her worked perfectly with it. I gravitated to her immediately with her big heart and the way she cares for others, and I admire her strength against all that is trying to bring her down. I'm looking at you, Keith. She was determined to come out on top and did just that. Her insecurities and soft heart just made her more layered and feel real. I would honestly love to be her friend.

The romance between Jackson and Delilah was utter perfection. They fit perfectly together, and I loved that they both showed their vulnerability and slowly opened up to one another. They talked about their innermost feelings, and one of my favorite things is that they actually truly listened to one another, taking their time to understand what they hide beneath 😌 Nothing felt rushed between them, and it felt real. I was having the best time with them, and their banter had me giggling like a schoolgirl.

I loved the side characters. The twins, Penelope and Adeline, were fun. The way that they cared about their brother, Jackson, and wanted to see him happy was the sweetest 🥹 I loved getting glimpses of Aiden and Lucie and how they helped make up the found family aspects.

If you're looking for a fun, cute read that is heartfelt, then look no further because this one right here is exactly that. I can't wait for the next one, which is Maggie and Copper.

Review of advance copy received from Netgalley
February 15, 2026
"There's very little I wouldn't do for you, Delilah."

"Demand more from me," I rasp. "I promise I'll
give it to you"

YES YES YES. I ATE THIS UP. NO DISAPPOINTMENT AT ALL AHHHHHH 🤭🤭

beware: long emotional ramble ahead because I have zero self-control when I love something this much 🫣🫣

I don’t even know where to start except to say this completely consumed my brain in the best way. From the very beginning I was locked in, like cancel-my-plans, ignore-my-responsibilities locked in. Something about the tone just felt cozy but charged (like sitting under a warm blanket while a snowstorm rattles the windows… see what i did there??😏). It had that banter that feels effortless instead of performative, and the emotional moments snuck up on me in a way that left my chest aching.

First things first, Jackson. I connected to him immediately because I’m also someone who runs on routine and organization, so I understood him from page one. 😭😭 But what really got me was how quietly attentive he is. A man who is good with kids is already dangerous territory for my heart, but the way he showed up for his sisters? I was done. Absolutely gone. And even when he was pretending not to like Delilah, he was always watching her, noticing things, making sure she was okay without making a show of it. I wanted to scream. Because YES WE LOVE A MAN WHO ISN’T NONCHALANT. Like make it obvious you notice 😮‍💨

”I know she sleeps with her hands tucked under her cheek, curled on her side.
She stole the extra quilt from my side of the bed, but I don't mind. I want her to be warm.”


And when I tell you this man’s love language is physical touch… always finding reasons to stay close, brushing her hair back, hands on her neck, her wrist, her ankle, like he just needed the contact to ground himself. The caretaking energy should honestly be classified as its own trope because I will eat that up every single time. He wasn’t just obsessed with her—he needed her.

“I squeeze her hips so hard I bet she’ll have fingertip-sized bruises tomorrow.
Ten perfect presses of blue and purple. The shape of my need for her.”


And Delilah… oh my heart hurt for her in a completely different way. At first it felt like life just kept knocking her sideways, and everyone had already decided who she was based on rumors and little mistakes that piled up into this unfair reputation. Meanwhile she’s trying so hard to be taken seriously and to hold everything together, especially with her grandfather being sick. 🥺🥺 Her softness could’ve been written as fragility, but instead it came across as strength—this stubborn optimism that refuses to die even when things keep going wrong. (ALSO!!!! I need to formally state my hatred for Keith. Worst boss ever. Straight to jail. Do not pass go. Do not collect $200. No redemption arc allowed.😾)

What really got me was how much pain both of them were carrying under the surface. Jackson’s anxiety and fear of letting people down had him clinging to routine like it was the only thing keeping him upright, 😔 and Delilah was carrying this quiet desperation to prove herself while feeling invisible at the same time.💔💔 But being thrown together forced them to confront those fears instead of hiding behind them, and in the process they ended up giving each other the reassurance neither of them knew how to ask for. The trip forced them into proximity in a way that stripped away their assumptions, and I loved how their dynamic shifted from irritation to friendship to something softer and heavier all at once. Somehow, without even trying, they became a safe place for each other to finally loosen their grip and breathe. And watching Delilah realize she was falling for him was so fun 🤭🤭 because it wasn’t instant… it was like she kept catching herself noticing things she wasn’t supposed to be noticing.

“Jackson is nice to look at and knows about cloud formations. Delilah catnip, basically.”


But out of everything my biggest highlight is between Jackson and his sisters. Seeing him finally understand that he didn’t fail them, that he was enough, that all his sacrifices actually mattered… I had tears in my eyes and I’m not even exaggerating. 😭😭😭

“Penelope and I have never missed a meal with you. You’ve never missed a doctor’s appointment or parent-teacher conference or dance recital. Why do I need a mom when I have a Jackson?”


By the end I just felt full in that bittersweet way where you’re so satisfied but also mourning because you’re not ready to leave these people yet.😭😭🥹 I loved the relationships, the quiet moments, the humor, the way it balanced heaviness with warmth. I genuinely didn’t want it to end, and now I’m just sitting here hoping the next story gives us more glimpses of them because I am not done.

[Also can we PLEASE talk about the side characters because I am already feral over the possibility of Maggie and Cooper. The tension??? The mystery??? The controlling, dark energy??? I am seated. I am waiting. I am unwell.]

Anyway, if you made it through this entire spiral of feelings, rambling, and me aggressively loving these characters… congratulations. You’ve essentially experienced the emotional aftermath right along with me. So thank you 🫶🏼🫶🏼 I can’t think of a better way to end this review than this…

And now, back to you, Goodreads.

Consider this my formal petition for more pathetic mmcs.

Jackson is so utterly pathetic & obsessed and I LOVED it! The world deserves more pathetic (complementary) men.

And Now, Back to You is an easy-to-binge, banter-filled, perfect to snuggle up with on a cold winter night, romance book. You should absolutely pick this one up while the weather is still right for optimal vibes.

B.K. Borison has yet to disappoint. This was fun, quick, and left me wanting more from this world. Her banter never misses and this one had me LOLing, and grinning non-stop.

I loved our two main characters and all their flaws. Delilah reminded me a little of myself when I was younger and perpetually masking. I’m so glad she found someone to love her and that she felt comfortable taking her shield down for. Thats what we all deserve, someone (romantic or platonic) that will love all our bits, not just the parts we share with the world.

Whats to love…
- opposites attract
- mommy trauma x2
- single caregiver MMC
- slutty little glasses
- snowed-in
- only one bed
- body heat to stay warm
- “let me take care of you” x2
- he’s pathetic and ridiculously down bad
- she’s “too much” & he likes her just as she is

What might not work for some…
- I can see it now, some readers are going to say this is insta-love, and maybe they’ll be right. But insta-love happens in real-life and this is a VERY believable, trauma-bonding, finally--someone I can be myself around, kind of insta-love. 1,000% these two stay together forever.
- I personally thought there was SO much potential for more vulnerability, emotional intimacy, and character development with these two that what we got felt surface level at times. It was still good, but the potential for more was screaming at me, and I wanted that more!

4.5⭐️| IG | TikTok |

“It’s always been me coming right back to you. You’re the end of every sentence, Delilah. I’ve just been too stubborn to see it.”😍

This was such a heartfelt and wonderful romance about finding your path in life, love, family and standing up for yourself. And Now, Back to You follows Jackson and Delilah who are both meteorologists and polar opposites of each other. But when they are partners for a snowstorm they have to find a way to collaborate. Together they make a deal if Jackson agrees to help Delilah be taken seriously then Delilah will help Jackson with showing his fun side. What will happen next?

"I think you hide all your best parts in tiny, little pouches, Jackson Clark."

Thoughts
I was invested in the story and the romance from the very first page. The plot kept me engaged and the pacing was perfect. The writing was easy to follow, descriptive and witty. I enjoyed the winter vibes and the sledding scene was super fun, it reminded me of my sledding adventures. Reading this book felt like a warm blanket in front of a fire. I felt many emotions while reading this book including happiness, sadness and anger. I appreciated that the author discussed important topics in a relatable way such as family issues, anxiety and job issues. The ending was heartwarming and I'm glad it ended on a happy note.

Characters
I loved Delilah she was spontaneous, independent, chaotic, resilient, brave and caring. I was so proud that Delilah stood up for herself and made sure that people took her seriously. I related to her because my great Aunt has Alzheimers similar to Delilah's grandpa although thankfully she remembers my name. I'm in love with Jackson, he was funny, hardworking, organized, sweet, nerdy and protective of his sisters. I loved that he rambled about the weather and the fact that he has glasses made me fall even more. I'm so glad that Jackson showed his serious side as well as his fun side and everything in between. The sledding scene made me giggle and blush so much! The side characters were great especially Penelope, and Adeline, Lucie, Aiden and Maggie. I loved Jackson's interactions with his sisters Penelope and Adeline. It reminded me of how close my sister and I are.

Romance
The romance was a bit insta-lust to me but I understood that the close proximity increased the timeline of their romance. The chemistry and tension between Delilah and Jackson was amazing! I'm glad that they actually talked about their feelings and thankfully there was no miscommunication. I loved that Delilah and Jackson were opposites but are great together. I adored that Jackson let Delilah be her own person but also helped when she needed it. Deckson forever!

I recommend this book to anyone who loves romance, awesome characters, and great chemistry between the main characters.

This book can basically be summed up in two points:
1. The title will be stuck in your head forever because it’s mentioned so many times.
2. Delilah needs to be wrapped in bubble wrap because she is a walking hazard.

Delilah’s character was tough for me to connect with. She’s a brilliant meteorologist on camera, but the second the cameras turn off, she becomes a total disaster. Watching her fumble through challenges that were easily fixable was frustrating. The central conflict that drove the entire plot felt flimsy, and Delilah desperately needed to find a backbone. Unfortunately, she didn’t find one for about 90% of the book.

As for the romance with Jackson… it felt forced. The two were opposites when it came to anything that wasn’t weather related. Which can be cute when written well, but here it wasn’t. Jackson’s entire purpose in life seemed to be holding Delilah’s hand and cleaning up her messes instead of pushing her to grow up.

To make things worse, Jackson is already raising his younger siblings, so he has more than enough responsibility. Dating Delilah just gave him another child to care for. Except this one’s an adult in theory, but not in behavior.

I really struggled to get through this one. I picked it up and put it down for weeks, hoping it would click eventually. I own multiple copies of First Caller because I loved it so my expectations for And Now Back To You were sky high. Good thing I have a parachute with me at all times for emergencies. This book did not meet my expectations, but it could find its right audience.

♾️⭐️!!

Dare I say that this might be one of my favorite books of all time? Cause it certainly feels like it. I genuinely feel like this book might be perfect, at least for me, and the way it made me feel the entire time I was reading it?? SWOONNNNNNN!

I just have to start this review by saying that Jackson and Delilah were perfection. Everything about them was perfection. Their banter? Their chemistry? Their feelings? *chefs kiss*
I felt myself really relating to Delilah from the very beginning with how she was so spontaneous and out there and just all around goofy and clumsy. She lacked quite a bit of confidence at the beginning, but once she started to feel the support of those around her and the fact that she really did have a voice, all the puzzle pieces fell together perfectly.

Jackson is by far, HANDS DOWN, my favorite book boyfriend ever. I could go on and on and on about this man because he was so generous, so sweet. He treated everyone in his life with such care that you could feel the love pouring from these pages.
How could you not fall in love with a man who raised his sisters to be the beautiful beings they are because their mother was completely absent?
How could you not fall in love with a man who cares most about you being comfortable and happy when it's freezing outside?
How could you not fall in love with a man who goes sledding with you simply because he wants to show you he loves you through small, spontaneous acts of kindness and fun?
Jackson is a true man, one with a kind heart and a perfect soul.

I believe the plot itself was also really well done! The idea of getting caught in a snowstorm while you have to report during it and who knows, you might fall in love with a cute weather boy on the way. It was so sweet and easy to binge this books and it only took a few odd hours once I sat down and got into this. This is one of those books that you don't realize you've read 100 pages until it's 2am and you forgot you set yourself a limit of 1 or 2 chapters before bed. It was THAT addictive.

Overall, I can't wait to display this series on my favorites shelf because this universe and these characters mean so much to me. Now, after reading these two books, I can confirm that it is light years ahead of the Lovelight series and would definitely recommend these two books if you want to try this author again. She has delivered banger after banger and I can't wait to she what she writes next!!
